sprites.title: 2D Explosion Animations #1
sprites.note: 8×8 frame grid, 256px cells. Frame-by-frame smoke and fire — the format our destruction FX should ship in.

sprites.title: 2D Explosion Animations #3
sprites.note: Same grid, different dissipation curve. Note how the last two rows are almost pure smoke.

sprites.title: 2D Explosion Animations #2 (set 2)
sprites.note: Directional blast. Useful for wall-breach and barrel spells.

sprites.title: Pixel FX Pack — impact
sprites.note: Pixel-art FX at a sane cell size; the resolution band we should actually work at.

sprites.title: Pixel FX Pack — burst
sprites.note: Radial burst timing: 3 fast frames in, 6 slow frames out.

sprites.title: Pixel FX Pack — smoke
sprites.note: Smoke puffs for rubble and footfalls.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Magic Pack — Lightning
sprites.note: Single-row strip sheet. Spell FX at true pixel resolution.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Magic Pack — Fire bomb
sprites.note: Projectile + detonation in one strip — the shape a 'break the wall' spell needs.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Magic Pack — Dark bolt
sprites.note: Travel loop then impact; note the tiny frame count that still reads.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Town — character atlas
sprites.note: A whole cast packed into one atlas — hero, enemies, props, all on one palette.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Town — tileset
sprites.note: The tile vocabulary a whole level is built from. Ours needs a damaged variant per tile.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Town — buildings
sprites.note: Destructible candidates: these read as brick/timber assemblies that could shed pieces.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Town — props
sprites.note: Barrels, lamps, fences — the small breakables that sell a destructible world.

sprites.title: Gothicvania Town — assembled scene
sprites.note: The same tiles composed into a level, so we can judge tile → scene.

sprites.title: Super Grotto — far parallax layer
sprites.note: Parallax layer 1 of 4. Low contrast, low detail, cool shift.

sprites.title: Super Grotto — mid parallax layer
sprites.note: Parallax layer 3 of 4 — where silhouette shapes start to bite.

sprites.title: Super Grotto — layers composited
sprites.note: All four layers stacked. This is the parallax depth budget we should copy.

sprites.title: Fort of Illusion — assembled scene
sprites.note: Stone fort kit at 3× — brick shapes we can plausibly shatter into chunks.

sprites.title: Forest of Illusion — assembled scene
sprites.note: Trees and bushes as discrete props — exactly the things a fire spell should fell.

sprites.title: Boss: Demon Slime — idle/attack
sprites.note: Large boss frames, ~120px tall, heavy squash and anticipation. Animation quality bar for our bosses.

sprites.title: Boss: Demon Slime — ground slam
sprites.note: Impact frame holds for 2–3 ticks, then dust. Copy this timing.

sprites.title: Boss: Demon Slime — cast
sprites.note: Telegraph → release → recovery, all clearly separated in silhouette.

sprites.title: Elementals: Fire Knight — run
sprites.note: 8-frame run cycle with cape follow-through.

sprites.title: Elementals: Fire Knight — attack
sprites.note: Sword arc drawn as a smear frame — cheap, and it sells the speed.

sprites.title: Hero Knight — combat
sprites.note: Note the low frame count per action; readability beats smoothness.

sprites.title: Huntress — animation set
sprites.note: Ranged-hero reference; bow draw and release poses.

sprites.title: Evil Wizard — cast
sprites.note: Caster silhouette: robe motion carries the whole animation.
